learningObjectives.title: The meaning and observance of festivals

questions.q: On which date do most Christians celebrate Christmas Day?
questions.explain: Christmas Day, celebrating the birth of Jesus, is observed on 25 December in the Western Church.

questions.q: The word 'Advent' comes from a Latin word meaning what?
questions.explain: 'Advent' derives from the Latin 'adventus', meaning 'coming', referring to the coming of Christ.

questions.q: When does the season of Advent begin?
options: On the fourth Sunday before Christmas
questions.explain: Advent starts on the fourth Sunday before Christmas and lasts until Christmas Eve.

questions.q: On which date is the festival of Epiphany celebrated?
questions.explain: Epiphany falls on 6 January, twelve days after Christmas.

questions.q: How many days does the season of Lent traditionally last?
questions.explain: Lent lasts forty days, mirroring the forty days Jesus spent fasting in the wilderness.

questions.q: Which day marks the first day of Lent?
questions.explain: Lent begins on Ash Wednesday, the day after Shrove Tuesday.

questions.q: Good Friday commemorates which event in the life of Jesus?
options: The crucifixion and death of Jesus
questions.explain: Good Friday remembers the crucifixion and death of Jesus on the cross.

questions.q: The word 'Maundy' in Maundy Thursday comes from a Latin word meaning what?
questions.explain: 'Maundy' comes from the Latin 'mandatum' (commandment), recalling Jesus' new commandment to love one another.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the season of Advent for Christians?
options: To prepare and wait for the coming of Christ
To mourn the death of Jesus
To give thanks for the harvest
questions.explain: Advent is a time of preparation and expectant waiting for the celebration of Christ's coming.

questions.q: Which event does the festival of Epiphany chiefly celebrate?
options: The visit of the Wise Men to the infant Jesus
The birth of Jesus in Bethlehem
The presentation of Jesus at the Temple
questions.explain: In the Western Church Epiphany celebrates the visit of the Magi (Wise Men) to Jesus.

questions.q: The forty days of Lent recall which event in Jesus' life?
options: Jesus spending forty days fasting in the wilderness
The forty days before his birth
questions.explain: Lent's length reflects the forty days Jesus fasted and was tempted in the wilderness.

questions.q: On Ash Wednesday, ashes are placed on believers' foreheads mainly to symbolise what?
questions.explain: The ashes are a sign of penitence and a reminder of human mortality at the start of Lent.

questions.q: Palm Sunday begins Holy Week and remembers which event?
questions.explain: Palm Sunday recalls Jesus riding into Jerusalem while crowds waved palm branches.

questions.q: Maundy Thursday chiefly commemorates which event?
questions.explain: Maundy Thursday remembers the Last Supper, when Jesus shared bread and wine with his disciples.

questions.q: Easter Sunday is significant for Christians because it celebrates what?
options: The resurrection of Jesus from the dead
The giving of the Holy Spirit
questions.explain: Easter Sunday celebrates the resurrection of Jesus, the central belief of the Christian faith.

questions.q: Why do many Christians regard Easter as the most important festival of the year?
options: Because the resurrection is central to Christian belief in life after death
Because it marks the start of the Church year
Because it is the oldest festival
questions.explain: The resurrection underpins Christian hope of eternal life, making Easter the most important festival.

questions.q: A family lights one extra candle on a wreath on each of the four Sundays before Christmas. What is this wreath called?
questions.explain: The Advent wreath has a candle for each Sunday of Advent, lit in turn as Christmas approaches.

questions.q: A Christian decides to give up eating chocolate for the forty days leading up to Easter. Which period are they observing?
questions.explain: Giving something up as self-discipline for the forty days before Easter is a common observance of Lent.

questions.q: A family eats pancakes to use up rich foods on the day before Lent begins. Which day are they marking?
questions.explain: Shrove Tuesday, or Pancake Day, uses up rich foods before the fasting of Lent begins.

questions.q: A Christian attends a sunrise service to celebrate Jesus rising from the tomb. Which festival are they observing?
questions.explain: Sunrise services on Easter Sunday celebrate the discovery of the empty tomb and Jesus' resurrection.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Christianity: Festivals & Fasts
